documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up (seen 2022-03-08)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — 03/08/2022

Central DI. Delivered in October; the third-trimester rise in thirst and urine output settled within a few weeks postpartum. Now back to her usual pattern on desmopressin 0.1 mg BID, nocturia 0–1. Postpartum sodium normal (PCP, December).

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.
Exam: normal.

Plan: continue current dose. Sodium yearly. Return in 1 year, sooner with any change.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Daughter is almost 8 months; pt back to full-time freelance design work from home, "juggling." Sleep improving.

Mood: more stressed. PHQ-9 10, mostly fatigue, concentration, feeling overwhelmed; item 9 = 0. Taking sertraline. Wants to try managing with more structure before changing anything.

DI: stable. Epilepsy: no seizures. HIV: ID visit coming up in August; admits she has been "less perfect" with Biktarvy since the baby — misses a dose here and there.

Meds: phenytoin ER 300 qHS, desmopressin 0.1 BID, Biktarvy daily, sertraline 100 daily, folic acid 1 mg, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa (anaphylaxis), latex.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gen well. HEENT ok. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs CTA. Abd soft. Ext no edema. Neuro nonfocal. Skin normal.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Pap not due (3 normal yearly; co-test 2023). Shingrix #1 today (recommended with HIV); #2 in 2 months. CBC, CMP, lipids, phenytoin level.
- ART adherence — talked about pairing Biktarvy with the baby's morning bottle; phone alarm. ID will check viral load.
- MDD, recurrent — mild-moderate symptoms. Continue sertraline 100; revisit in the fall, sooner if worse.
- DI, epilepsy — stable.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal — blood count, kidney, liver, sodium, cholesterol. Phenytoin level is in range. Shingrix #2 is due around August 16.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up (seen 2022-08-09)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, 08/09/2022

First visit since delivery (missed the January appointment). She acknowledges missed Biktarvy doses — "a couple a week" — since the baby. No fevers, no thrush, weight stable.

Labs: HIV RNA 1,240 copies/mL (previously undetectable). CD4 276 cells/uL (down from 401).

Allergies: SULFONAMIDES — anaphylaxis; latex.

Assessment: low-level viremia from missed doses. No resistance testing at this level; will repeat.
Plan: adherence counseling with our pharmacist; daily phone reminder; pill box. Continue Biktarvy. Repeat viral load in 6–8 weeks, then visit in 3 months.

ID attending

documents.title: Shingrix Dose 2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Arm sore after first dose for a day, nothing else. Series complete.

documents.title: Refill — phenytoin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: phenytoin ER 100 mg #270. Per pharmacy, last 90-day fill was early May. Refill approved per protocol. Left message for pt to call — PCP would like to know if she has been missing doses; offered blister packaging through the pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Refill — phenytoin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt returned call. Says she had "a stash" from the spring and is taking it every night. Agreed to blister packs for phenytoin and desmopressin. Pharmacy updated.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid and Pfizer bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Latex-free bandages.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up mood and meds. ID letter reviewed: viral load 1,240 and CD4 276 in August from missed doses; she says the repeat was "better" and she is using an alarm now. Blister packs for phenytoin and desmopressin since September.

Mood lower since late summer — tired, not enjoying things the way she did, guilt about "not doing enough" for her daughter, short on sleep. Working. Appetite ok. PHQ-9 12. Denies SI or thoughts of self-harm. No psychosis. Taking sertraline daily.

O: vitals as charted. Tired-appearing, good eye contact, affect constricted but reactive. Speech normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. MDD, recurrent, moderate symptoms now. She would like counseling first; referral to behavioral health (telehealth therapist through her plan). Keep sertraline 100 for now. Revisit 6–8 weeks; call/portal anytime. Crisis line info given.
2. Med adherence — blister packs, alarms. Good.
3. Epilepsy, DI — stable.
4. Flu/COVID done 10/11.

documents.title: Behavioral Health Intake (seen 2023-01-05)
documents.author: behavioral health
documents.body:
Community behavioral health — intake summary, 01/05/2023 (telehealth).

Referred for recurrent depression. 32-year-old graphic designer, single mother of a 14-month-old, lives with a roommate. Current symptoms: low mood, fatigue, guilt, poor sleep. Denies suicidal ideation, intent or plan; no history of attempts. No substance use. On sertraline through PCP.

Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, recurrent.
Plan: weekly individual CBT-based therapy, telehealth. Will coordinate with PCP as needed.

Licensed clinical social worker

events.reason: Seizure with fall from second-story window

conditions.label: Traumatic brain injury with bilateral cerebral contusions and small intraventricular hemorrhage
Patient's intentional underdosing of medication regimen
conditions.note: Stopped all medications before the 2023-05-11 seizure

reports.text: Indication: seizure with fall from height, obtunded. Technique: noncontrast axial CT of the head with multiplanar reformats. Findings: Contusions in both cerebral hemispheres. Small volume of intraventricular hemorrhage. No extra-axial collection. No midline shift. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium and skull base intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral cerebral contusions with a small intraventricular hemorrhage. No skull fracture.

reports.text: Comparison: 5/11/2023. Bilateral cerebral contusions and small intraventricular hemorrhage are unchanged in extent. No new hemorrhage. No hydrocephalus. No midline shift.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (2023-05-11)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — physician record, 05/11/2023 21:40

Arrived by EMS. 32-year-old woman with generalized epilepsy since childhood and central diabetes insipidus (worse during her pregnancy in 2021) who had a seizure witnessed by her roommate and fell from a second-floor window. Roommate tells us she has had seizures since she was a child and stopped taking her medicines recently.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.

On arrival: postictal, obtunded. T 36.5 C, HR 108, BP 138/90. Respirations irregular. Pupils sluggish to light. No purposeful response to pain; decerebrate posturing. Reflexes brisk. Intubated for airway protection (rapid sequence).

Trauma survey: no long-bone deformity, pelvis stable, chest and abdomen without injury on primary and secondary survey and on imaging.

Isotonic saline 120 mL given over the first two hours; urine output over that time 1.4 L via Foley.

Labs: Na 151, serum osm 302, urine SG 1.002, urine osm 68, glucose 110. Phenytoin level undetectable.

CT head: bilateral cerebral contusions and small intraventricular hemorrhage.

Impression: breakthrough generalized seizure from antiseizure medication nonadherence, with fall from height and traumatic brain injury (bilateral contusions, small IVH); hypernatremia with dilute high-volume urine — uncontrolled central DI off desmopressin.
Plan: fosphenytoin load, desmopressin, neurosurgery and neurology consults, admit neuro ICU.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (05/11–05/22/2023)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/11/2023 (neuro ICU) — discharged 05/22/2023.

Diagnoses:
1. Generalized tonic-clonic seizure due to stopping antiseizure medication
2. Traumatic brain injury — bilateral cerebral contusions, small intraventricular hemorrhage (fall from second story during seizure)
3. Hypernatremia from uncontrolled central diabetes insipidus (missed desmopressin)
4. Medication nonadherence (had stopped all home medications)
5. HIV on ART; recurrent major depression

Course: Loaded with fosphenytoin, then phenytoin resumed at home dose. Desmopressin given IV initially; urine output fell and sodium normalized gradually over about 48 hours with free water. Neurosurgery followed — nonoperative. Repeat head CT at 24 h stable. Extubated hospital day 3, then transferred to the floor. No further seizures. Mental status improved steadily; at discharge alert, oriented, conversant, ambulating independently. PT/OT cleared for home with roommate. She told the team she stopped her pills a few weeks ago because she was "tired of being a patient"; social work and the inpatient psychiatry liaison met with her — no SI; sertraline resumed.

Allergies: SULFONAMIDES (anaphylaxis); LATEX.

Discharge medications (home regimen resumed): phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; desmopressin 0.1 mg BID; Biktarvy 1 tab daily; sertraline 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.

Instructions: no driving for 6 months after the seizure (Massachusetts rule); no heights, bathing alone or swimming alone. Follow up with PCP within 1 week, neurology 4 weeks, endocrinology, ID.

Hospitalist

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call 2 days after discharge. Pt home with roommate and daughter. Has all meds; roommate set up a weekly pill box and watches her take the night doses. Mild fatigue. No seizures, no vomiting, thirst normal. Appointment with PCP 5/30. Discharge records received and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up (TCM).

Admitted 5/11–5/22 after a seizure with fall from a second-story window: bilateral cerebral contusions and small IVH, nonoperative; hypernatremia from uncontrolled DI; she had stopped all of her medications a few weeks before. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Today: here with roommate. Tired, but thinking clearly. No seizures since. Taking everything — roommate watches night doses. Thirst normal again. No vomiting. When I asked about stopping the meds she said she was "sick of the pills and the appointments" and missed the April visit for the same reason. Low but not hopeless; PHQ-9 10, item 9 zero. Still seeing her therapist by video, though she had skipped a few sessions in the spring.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, oriented x3, speech fluent. Pupils equal and reactive. CN intact. Strength and sensation normal and symmetric. Finger-nose normal. Gait steady. Heart RRR, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. TBI with bilateral contusions/IVH — recovering, nonfocal exam. Neurology 6/20. Avoid driving 6 months; no ladders, baths alone.
2. Seizure from stopping phenytoin — resumed. Level and BMP today.
3. Central DI — back on desmopressin.
4. Medication nonadherence — big picture talk; pill box, blister packs, roommate support; she agrees to message me before stopping anything.
5. MDD, recurrent — moderate; continue sertraline 100 + therapy; follow up 4–6 weeks.
6. HIV — needs ID visit; she'll call.

documents.title: Labs after the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium is normal now and your phenytoin level is back in the therapeutic range. Keep going exactly as you are. Neurology is June 20.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up (seen 2023-06-20)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology — 06/20/2023

Seen after admission for a breakthrough generalized seizure (first since 2017) after she stopped phenytoin, with fall from height and bilateral cerebral contusions plus small IVH. No seizures since restarting. Back on phenytoin 300 mg nightly; level therapeutic on 5/30.

Exam: normal mental status, cranial nerves, motor, sensory, coordination and gait.

Allergies: sulfonamides, latex.

Plan: continue phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS. No driving until 11/11/2023 (six months seizure-free). Seizure precautions. Return in 1 year, sooner with any event.

documents.title: letter for a client
documents.author: patient
documents.body: One of my bigger clients wants a note that I was in the hospital in May and can work again. Nothing medical in it please. Thank you!

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Gretchen Kelleher was hospitalized from May 11 to May 22, 2023, and was unable to work during that time. She has recovered and may return to her usual work without restrictions as of June 1, 2023.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up (seen 2023-07-18)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology — 07/18/2023

Central DI. Hospitalized in May with hypernatremia (Na 151) after stopping desmopressin, in the setting of a seizure and TBI. Back on desmopressin 0.1 mg BID since; sodium normal 5/30. Thirst controlled.

We reviewed what happens off the drug and the need to keep a supply on hand. Medical alert bracelet recommended (epilepsy, DI).

Plan: continue current dose. Sodium every 6 months. Return 1 year.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up (seen 2023-09-12)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, 09/12/2023

First ID visit since the May hospitalization (seizure/TBI after stopping all medicines). She restarted Biktarvy at discharge but admits it is still "on and off" — the roommate supervises evening meds, but Biktarvy is a morning pill.

Labs: HIV RNA 8,900 copies/mL. CD4 214 cells/uL.

Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (anaphylaxis); latex.

Assessment: HIV with ongoing viremia from inconsistent adherence. CD4 just above the prophylaxis threshold.
Plan: move Biktarvy to bedtime with her phenytoin so it is part of the supervised routine. Return 3 months. If CD4 falls below 200 we will need Pneumocystis prophylaxis — note TMP-SMX is contraindicated (anaphylaxis).

ID attending

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical.

Interval: May admission (seizure/fall, bilateral contusions + small IVH, hypernatremia, had stopped meds). Neurology 6/20 normal exam; no driving until 11/11. Endocrinology 7/18 stable. ID 9/12: VL 8,900, CD4 214 — Biktarvy moved to bedtime with phenytoin.

She feels back to herself cognitively — working full days again. No seizures. Mood "so-so," PHQ-9 9; therapy every other week. Taking sertraline. Night meds supervised by roommate.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gen well. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Breasts no masses. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, co-test collected. Neuro: nonfocal, gait normal.

A/P:
- TBI — recovered clinically; resolved on problem list.
- Pap/HPV co-test today; if negative, next in 3 years (2026).
- Vaccines: flu, updated COVID, PCV20 (five years after PPSV23).
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids.
- HIV — viremic; ID managing; reinforced bedtime dosing.
- MDD — stable-ish; continue sertraline + therapy.
- Epilepsy, DI — stable.
